If root working mode is active, unlock all features below the KernelSU surface. 5) Include several root only features that can be altered using su or sui commands, or any other method that is mostly safe from causing boot loop but gives user those added privileges and access. 6) If root working mode is active, include SU mode access in terminal and ADB console. 7) In the Task Manager tab , if root working mode is active, include root only features to tweak CPU / GPU / RAM / Battery / Processes. 8) If root working mode is active, add additional options in the RRO/Monet Customization tab that are available to root only, identical to features available in the FOSS application Colorblendr (https://github.com/Mahmud0808/ColorBlendr.git) such as optional selection of custom secondary and tertiary accents. Include backup and restore. 9) If Root working mode is active, include an intent fire wall in the single application menu and batch application menu. .

node.content-desc:
Text note. Attached is the Hex Next repo that so far has been put together by using Google Argon 4 with mostly Kotlin. However, nothing works yet and it's all fragmented. In the Hex Next Folder that I attached, are screenshots of the Hex Next UI designed in Googles AI studio. Also in that folder are all the dozens of Hex Plugin APK's that offer countless theming options. Nothing has been updated beyond One UI 6.1.1 due to Samsung locking down RROs in One UI 7 preventing custom theming with ADB over UID 2000.
This application will utilize Superuser or Shizuku over UID 0 or 1000 to build overlays from scratch to replace the default SemWT_* overlays that were introduced beginning in One UI 7. With privilege escalation, the overlays can be built with maximum precedence to display over the default built in system overlays.
In the attached folder named Hex, you'll find screenshots of the UI built in Kotlin to help give you ideas. You don't have to use it, you can use whatever method is the most user friendly and looks the best.
The application should be able to determine the devices One UI version automatically and adjust it's theme build engine accordingly based on the differences between One UI 7, 8, and 9. Quick settings overlays are the most drastically changed. Therefore, keeping quick settings theming light would be wise with quick tile themes, but nothing fixed that would break compatability. Notification theming should be included. Most other One UI elements are for the most part unchanged with perhaps minor adjustments across One UI versions.
Drop theming for anything that isn't One UI and isn't built into the system. Samsung Messages is depracated. Other Samsung applications are okay to theme.
I want all the Hex Plugin theme options implemented into this single application. All the wallpapers, backgrounds, icon styles, .PNG icons, icon customization options, notification options, status bar options, everything brought in and updated to be compatible with One UI 7, 8, and 9. Start with One UI 9 compatability first so i can test on my phone. We can add compatability for One UI 7 and 8 once we have a working model.
Theming should include a simple and advanced mode. In simple mode, the user can select a theme plugin from the dozens of options and then go through each theme element and decide to turn that overlay element off or customize it with the various options that plugin allows. In advanced theme mode, all the simple mode options exist, but each component or overlay can be further themed by selecting a different plugin for each one and customizing overlays that way. Some of the plugins have beautiful .PNG options so I want them all added to the application so the user can decide which ones to use for the settings dashboard, file manager, power menu, etc.
Create an automatic safe mode fallback feature if the system crashes after implementing the built overlays.
Include a log of all the overlays being built and if any overlays fail, implement a fix and repair feature if possible.
Any Samsung applications that were debloated from the device should be automatically grayed out and not be included in building the overlays.
.
